summary: Case list with filtering, sorting and counts needs persistent storage and a new API; HLD designs the schema and endpoints, breakdown splits UI from backend, critic ensures consistency across specs.

steps.why: Convert the ticket into structured requirements with clear Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
Design the case storage schema, the list/count API endpoints, and how cases survive restarts.
steps.instructions: Focus on the database schema for case persistence, the REST API contract for list/filter/count operations, and how case state is preserved across restarts.

steps.why: Split into separate stories for backend (persistence, API) and any frontend integration.
steps.instructions: Consider separating storage/API implementation from any UI changes; each should be independently testable.

steps.why: Provide file-by-file implementation plans for the storage layer, API endpoints, and query building.
steps.instructions: Detail the database migration, repository pattern for case queries, API route handlers, and filter/sort query construction.

steps.why: Map test cases to each AC, especially pagination edge cases, filter combinations, and restart persistence.
steps.instructions: Cover pagination boundaries, filter combinations, sort ordering, count accuracy, and post-restart state verification.

steps.why: Loop feature_with_architecture: Deterministic merged_plan.md from ordered specs and story summaries.
Cross-check that the schema in HLD matches what breakdown and LLDs describe, and that all ACs trace through.
steps.instructions: Verify the database schema is consistent across HLD and stories, API contracts match in all documents, and every AC has corresponding tests.

steps.why: Human approval of specs and this plan before Dev.

skipped.why: Scope and acceptance criteria are clear and fully technical; no product ambiguity or user-facing decisions need product sign-off.
